title: 5 Hair-Care Mistakes You're Probably Making (And What To Do Instead)
description: If your hair feels dry, frizzy or just never quite right — one of these common mistakes could be the reason. Here's what to fix.
pinterestDescription: Is your hair always dry, frizzy or dull? You might be making one of these 5 very common hair-care mistakes. Here's exactly what to do instead. #haircare #hairtips #frizzyhair
author: Elevated Editorial
content:
Why Your Hair Never Seems Right

Most hair problems come down to a small set of very fixable mistakes. The good news is that once you identify which one applies to you, the fix is usually simple and affordable.

Mistake 1: Washing Your Hair Too Often

Daily washing strips the natural oils your scalp produces to protect and condition your hair. This is one of the most common causes of dry, frizzy and fragile hair — especially for people with naturally dry or curly hair.

What to do instead: Try extending your wash cycle. If you currently wash daily, try every other day for two weeks and see how your hair responds. Use a dry shampoo on non-wash days to manage roots.

Mistake 2: Rubbing Your Hair With a Towel

The rough motion of towel-drying creates significant friction on the hair cuticle, leading to frizz and breakage. This is especially damaging for wavy and curly hair types.

What to do instead: Gently squeeze — never rub — the water out of your hair with a microfibre towel or an old cotton t-shirt. Both are much gentler on the hair shaft.

Mistake 3: Using Heat Without Heat Protectant

Applying a flat iron or blow dryer to dry, unprotected hair is one of the fastest ways to cause long-term damage. The heat literally breaks down the protein structure of the hair strand.

What to do instead: Always apply a heat protectant spray or serum before any heat styling. Allow the product to absorb for 60 seconds before applying heat.

Mistake 4: Skipping Scalp Care

Your scalp is the foundation of healthy hair. Ignoring it — whether through product buildup, dryness or poor circulation — directly impacts the health of the hair that grows from it.

What to do instead: Incorporate a gentle scalp massage into your wash routine (even just 2–3 minutes). Look for shampoos formulated for your specific scalp type, not just your hair type.

Mistake 5: Overlapping Chemical Treatments

Colouring, bleaching, relaxing and keratin treatments all put significant stress on hair. Stacking multiple chemical processes in a short timeframe is a common cause of severe breakage.

What to do instead: Space chemical treatments at least 4–6 weeks apart. During this time, focus on protein treatments and deep conditioning to restore strength before the next process.

The Simple Fix

You don't need an expensive overhaul. Most hair improvements come from small consistent changes: washing less often, being gentler when wet, and always protecting before heat. Start with one change at a time and give it two weeks to notice a difference.
